headline: NPS River Use and Campground Reservation Requirements
reservation: Reservations for developed campgrounds like Round Spring or Pulltite must be made via Recreation.gov. River permits for private floating are not currently required, but organized outfitter shuttles should be booked in advance; check official NPS pages for updated seasonal management plans.

days.title: The Upper Current River

stops.name: Montauk State Park
stops.detail: Explore the headwaters of the Current River where seven springs merge to form a legendary trout stream.

stops.name: Akers Ferry
stops.detail: Observe the last operating current-driven ferry on the river and access key paddling launch points.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; travel involves winding two-lane highways.
days.note: River conditions change daily; consult the Akers Visitor Center for current hazards or fallen timber reports.

days.title: Spring-Fed Wonders

stops.name: Big Spring
stops.detail: Witness one of the world's largest springs as it emerges from the base of a limestone bluff into a turquoise pool.

stops.name: Rocky Falls
stops.detail: Visit this unique igneous shut-in where water cascades over ancient purple rhyolite into a large natural pool.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours; conditions vary on rural county roads.
days.note: Rocky Falls is a popular swimming site; arrive early during summer months to secure a picnic spot.

days.title: Caves and Confluences

stops.name: Round Spring Cavern
stops.detail: Join a ranger-led lantern tour to see delicate karst formations in an undeveloped cave setting.

stops.name: Jacks Fork River
stops.detail: Paddle or walk near the bluffs of this intimate tributary, known for its clear water and towering limestone walls.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; local transfers depend on outfitter shuttle schedules.
days.note: Cavern tours have limited capacity and are seasonally offered; verify the current schedule at the Round Spring ranger station.

intel.title: River Access Points
intel.text: Parking at popular landings like Waymeyer or Two Rivers can fill by 10 AM on summer Saturdays. Plan for shuttle drops to avoid parking congestion at the river's edge.

intel.title: Deep Valley Dead Zones
intel.text: Radio and cellular signals are almost non-existent once you descend into the river valley. Carry a physical map and establish a firm meeting time with your shuttle provider.

intel.title: Gateway Provisions
intel.text: Van Buren and Eminence serve as the primary hubs for fuel and ice. Stock up entirely before heading to remote campgrounds like Pulltite or Akers.

intel.title: Float Duration
intel.text: Allow 4–6 hours for a standard 10-mile float, accounting for stops at gravel bars. River speed varies significantly based on recent rainfall and spring discharge.

intel.title: Cave Safety
intel.text: Access to wild caves is restricted to prevent the spread of White-nose Syndrome. Only enter caves like Round Spring Cavern through official NPS-guided programs.

plan.arrival: Collect supplies in Springfield or Rolla. Proceed to the Van Buren or Eminence visitor centers to confirm river levels and outfitter locations before checking into your site.
plan.vehicle: High-clearance vehicles are advantageous for reaching remote river accesses. Check rental policies regarding travel on unpaved or gravel river landing roads.
plan.goldenHour: Alley Mill viewpoint offers a classic silhouette against the spring during the late afternoon, though shadows fall early in the deep valley.
